rationale: Round 1 built and ran cleanly, so I raised obfuscation pressure on the passes that hide this program's core structure — a tiny, arithmetic-dense FP loop — while still throttling the runtime-heavy ones. SUB and ICALL get the highest Security/Diversity weights because SUB obscures the floating-point expression chains that dominate flops-2 and ICALL hides the call/branch relationships, both at low semantic risk; FLA is kept strong since flattening the loop-heavy control flow is the best single reversal barrier and round 1 showed no stability issues. SPLIT stays weighted (cheap, low-risk, good diversity amplifier for the other passes). BCF is held back on RuntimeCost (0.35) because this is a tight FP throughput benchmark where bogus-control-flow re-entry tax is the steepest, but not zero so the framework can still select it where features favor it. IGV is mostly irrelevant here (only 2 functions, minimal globals), so it stays low across dimensions to effectively disable it. All CorrectnessRisk weights remain high since round 1 confirmed the pipeline is stable on this sample, keeping the door open for stronger selections without regression.
